chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a man who said to his mother, "Any woman I marry is as forbidden to me as you are." He said, "This is nothing."

key_terms.أَتَزَوَّجُهَا: I marry her, indicating a future marital contract
key_terms.أُمِّهِ: his mother, used here as the standard of permanent prohibition
key_terms.امْرَأَةٍ: a woman, referring to any woman he may marry
key_terms.لَيْسَ هَذَا بِشَيْءٍ: this is nothing, meaning it has no legal consequence

ai.seo_question: Does saying that one's future wife is like one's mother make marriage forbidden in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a man who utters a formula likening future wives to his mother in prohibition. Imam Abu Abdullah عليه السلام rules that such a statement has no legal effect and does not establish a valid prohibition.
